page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number 2 at left. Below it, a narrow marginal note column on the left with notes; the main text is a single column on the right, ending with a catchword-free last line "minatæ." Notes in the left margin, including a reference "Aug. de Ci. l. 1 c. 18. 1" at the foot of the margin.

main_text.p: fis de Deo, de Christo male, diuque solicitam habuit ; nu hæc diftra-ctio, quæ hodie est in Republica Christiana, originem ducit. ἀχμὴν vero & senectam paulo leuior quædam de nobismetipsis exercet velitatio: quæ tamen tanto maiores vbique tumultus ciet indies, quanto quisque se impensiùs quam Deum diligit : Reliqua quotquot vspiam terrarum occurrunt alias ζητήματα, ἐεσωὰν ἐνδὲν: De nostra, deque Romana Ecclesia ita plærique mihi perperam sentire videntur, quasi duæ semper ab origine sui fuissent, tempore ac loco, non secus ac Babylon & Hierosolyma, duæ vè illæ celebratissimæ Augustino ciuitates, palàm dister-minatæ.

page.notes: The marginal note at the top left is partly damaged; "nu hæc diftra-ctio" and the Greek words in the text are doubtful. The Greek fragments "ἀχμὴν", "ἐεσωὰν ἐνδὲν" and "ζητήματα" are uncertain. The reference at the foot of the left margin is partly illegible. Catchword and signature absent.
